text: {"score":2,"justification":"The core numbers match the card, but several claims are unsupported or misread, and some cited claims do not fit the sentences citing them. An investigator would have to redo part of the analysis.","problems":["The headline says 99215 is 'well above expectation in every complexity band'. The card shows only the provider's share in each band against the all-provider share, not against an expected share, and the claim 'sampled charts all support the billed level' ignores that a 99213 claim was documented below billed.","It says the mix is 'heavily weighted toward 99214', calling this a pattern that would concern a reviewer. 572 of 829 claims are 99214, but the card gives no peer comparison for 99214, so the concern is unsupported and contradicts the 99215 framing.","It states 'The repeated-time rate is notable', but no repeated-time figure appears on the card and nothing grounds it. The same applies to 'cloned text or repeated time entries'.","It says C0185318 'also appears among the late notes', and cites 'note checks' (problems 4%, late 9%) with no visible grounding. The card lacks note-level late flags, so this is probably unsupported.","The claims C0185668 and C0185909 are described as carrying 'only symptom or acute codes'. That fits R21 and R10.9, but C0185341 carries N39.0 (a UTI), which is not a symptom code. The claim-by-claim justification is loose.","It says the share runs 'two to four times' the all-provider rate for zero or one condition. The card gives 0.064/0.018 = 3.6 and 0.085/0.028 = 3.0, so 'two to four' is imprecise but acceptable.","The next step asks for charts starting with C0185361, a documented 99213 claim, mixed with the 99215 low-complexity claims. It also re-requests the audit trail without saying that no audit trail was received, and it is unclear whether one was ever requested.","It says 0 of 18 documented 99215 claims were below billed, 'against 9% for the comparison providers'. This matches the card's 0.087 all-provider rate. Yet the 'sampled' 45 charts are described as supporting the billed level in the headline, which overstates the documentation result given about 5% coverage."]}
